newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: East Zaire troubles spread, UN reports new attacks.
newsitem.headline: East Zaire troubles spread, UN reports new attacks.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency on Monday reported fresh troubles in east Zaire's volatile Goma region while nearly 250,000 Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees fled camps in nearby Uvira amid fighting between troops and rebels.
The Geneva-based UNHCR said it had unconfirmed reports of dead and wounded following a series of attacks on Sunday by unidentified gunmen in Goma.

Goma region, bordering Rwanda and home to 700,000 Rwandan Hutus who fled after 1994's genocide of Tutsis, is a tinderbox of rival ethnic groups. Hundreds of people have died in recent months in fighting between native Zairean tribes and Hutus.

UNHCR spokeswoman Christiane Berthiaume said one Zairean army officer of the U.N.-paid camp security contingent died and a Zairean soldier was wounded in a dawn attack on a UNHCR base near a sprawling Rwandan refugee camp in east Zaire on Sunday.
The identity of the attackers at the base near Katale camp, home to 202,000 Rwandan Hutus, was not known, she said.

Also on Sunday morning, unidentified gunmen attacked the town of Bunagana near eastern Zaire's border with Uganda and sporadic shooting was reported close to Kibumba refugee camp home to 190,000 Rwandan Hutus, near Rwanda's mountainous border.
Hours later the same day, gunmen attacked villages near another Rwandan refugee camp in the region, Kahindo, home to 112,000 people, the spokeswoman said.
All aid traffic in the region was then suspended and expatriates told to stay home.
"We have unconfirmed reports of dead and wounded. We have reports that the hospital in Katale town is full of the wounded," said Berthiaume.
UNHCR had no other details on the attacks or the motives, she said.

Aid sources in the region said the attackers had entered Zaire from Rwanda and struck government army positions close to Rwandan refugee camps near Goma. A senior aid official said there was a "sizeable military incursion from Rwanda".

The reports could not be confirmed independently and Rwanda's Tutsi-led army, which swept to power after the genocide of more than half a million minority Tutsis and Hutu moderates, could not be reached for comment.
In Geneva, a senior aid official said: "There are so many groups who could benefit from creating chaos in the region. There is complete confusion."
In Uvira region further to the south, Berthiaume said nearly 250,000 Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees had abandoned their 12 camps.

The army is battling ethnic Tutsi rebels in Uvira, where Berthiaume said some 221,000 refugees were on the move towards another eastern Zairean town, Bukavu, already cut off from Uvira by the Banyamulenge Tutsi rebels.
